sources.what: Gregory the Great, Moralia XXXI.xlv (§§87–91, on Job 39:25: the seven principal vices, pride their queen)
sources.translator: Library of the Fathers, 'Morals on the Book of Job', vol. III pt 2 (Oxford, 1850); translator not named on the page (the LF Moralia is usually credited to James Bliss and Charles Marriott)
sources.note: Page checked: Book XXXI ch. xlv, beginning 'For the tempting vices, which fight against us in invisible contest'. PLEASE CHECK the page reproduces the 1844–50 LF text (it names no translator); archive.org scans of the LF volume are searched as a fallback. Job journey uses other parts of the Moralia: no overlap.

sources.note: For the lecture and background (the eight thoughts as the West received them). Evagrius has no confirmed public-domain English: our own words.

art.why: Bosch's Seven Deadly Sins is in the Prado; no NGA painting of the sins together in the open data.

art.title: Mountain Landscape with Bridge
art.why: 'A mountain': travellers crossing a bridge towards hills and mountains in the distance, for Dante's mountain to be climbed. Cole's Notch of the White Mountains was claimed by is-god-coming-back.

art.title: The Fall of Phaeton
art.why: 'A proud figure humbled': the boy who drove the sun's chariot falling headfirst, the classical picture of pride's fall.

art.title: A Sleeping Girl
art.why: 'A sleeping figure': the lecture can say that sloth is not sleep but not caring; the painting is only of sleep. (Inman's Rip Van Winkle is an alternative.)

art.title: Ill-Matched Lovers
art.why: Lust and avarice in one picture: the gallery's description has the old man's embrace, the woman holding a leather pouch, a fool reaching for it, and coins on the ledge. Bosch's Death and the Miser is already used.

music.why: Spec's choice: Psalm 51 sung, the prayer of a heart that has looked in the mirror.
